title: Pólya's Recurrence Theorem
objective: The viewer understands why a randomly wandering walker is certain to return to its start in two dimensions, yet has only about a one-in-three chance of ever returning in three, and sees the one-line reason (the return probabilities sum to infinity in 2D and to a finite number in 3D).
audience: Curious technical viewers on short-form social: comfortable with basic probability and series, no measure theory. They know what a random walk is only loosely.

message.core_message: A random walk on a lattice returns home with certainty in 1D and 2D but only with probability about 0.34 in 3D, because the chance of being home at step 2n decays like 1/n in 2D (sum diverges) and like n^(-3/2) in 3D (sum converges).
key_points: The drunk man (2D grid, 4 directions) returns to his door with probability 1, though the expected wait is infinite.
The drunk bird (3D lattice, 6 directions) returns with probability about 0.3405, so it never returns about 66% of the time.
Polya (1921): the simple random walk on Z^d is recurrent for d = 1, 2 and transient for d >= 3.
Reason: P(at origin at step 2n) ~ 1/(pi n) in 2D and ~ 2 (3/(4 pi n))^(3/2) in 3D; the expected number of returns is the sum of these.
The model is idealised: unbiased, independent steps on an infinite lattice. It is a statement about mathematics, not about real birds.

avoid: cartoon or clip-art drunks and birds
claiming the bird is certain to be lost

constraints: Pitch black (#000) canvas; the dark-tech style with the paper colour overridden.
Readable with sound off: every narrated claim has an on-screen statement.
Every plotted or drawn walk is a real seeded simulation; numbers come from the verified research dossier.
Narration never plays over a static frame.

research.reason: Mathematical claims (recurrence in 2D, transience in 3D, return probability 0.3405, asymptotic return odds) must be checked against the literature.

creative_directions.name: Pitch-black instrument panel
creative_directions.concept: The film is a measuring instrument pointed at one question: does the walker come back? A faint lattice and monospace readouts (step count, dimension, returns) frame two real simulated walkers, blue for the man in 2D and amber for the bird in 3D. Paths are drawn with a bright leading dot and a persistent trail so the viewer sees the wandering, the loops and, for the man, the return pulse at his door. The theorem is then shown as data: a table of dimensions with return probabilities, and two log-scale plots whose curves separate (diverging versus converging sum).

visual_identity.palette: #000000 canvas, #f0f6fc ink, #8b949e secondary ink, #21262d rules; blue #58a6ff = 2D man, amber #e3b341 = 3D bird, green #3fb950 = returned home, red #f85149 = escaped.
visual_identity.typography: Inter 700 for statements, JetBrains Mono for readouts, labels and formulae.
visual_identity.texture: None. Flat black with hairline lattice rules and corner brackets.

signature_moves: mono step counter running with the walk
hairline draw-on for grids and plots
single pulse ring when a walker reaches home
motion_language.transitions: Short crossfades between scenes with the lattice persisting as a visual anchor; no whooshes.

composition.approach: Portrait only: statement and readout above, a 600x600 stage in the optical centre, tally and caveat below, all inside the portrait safe area.

creative_directions.pacing: Walks run at 30 to 60 steps per second so the viewer reads individual steps; a new element or change lands at least every 2 to 3 seconds.
creative_directions.why_it_fits: It matches the technical, instrument-like brief and lets the maths itself be the spectacle.

creative_directions.name: Typographic proof (considered, not chosen)
creative_directions.concept: A text-led film: the theorem and its series argument typeset large on black with only small inset walk diagrams, closer to a lecture slide than an instrument. Clear for the maths, but the man and bird scenarios become illustrations of the formula instead of the evidence for it.

visual_identity.palette: #000000 canvas with white type and a single accent.
visual_identity.typography: Inter 700 display with JetBrains Mono formulae.

creative_directions.why_it_fits: Rejected because the brief asks to demonstrate the two scenarios first; the walks need to be the main visual.

success_criteria: Hook states the contrast (one gets home, one may not) within the first 8 seconds.
Man scenario shows a real walk returning home; bird scenario shows a real walk that does not.
The theorem statement and the 1/n versus n^(-3/2) reason are each on screen long enough to read.
Every scene is legible at phone size and inside the portrait safe area.
The ending holds for at least 2 seconds.
